units.spine: On market day Rundgate is most itself, and the trade that comes into the town is the reason the stalls go up.
Armed order is part of how Rundgate is kept, and the town pays professionals for its safety rather than leaning on luck or its neighbours.
People in Rundgate have enough that their arguments are rarely about money.
There is nothing about Rundgate that looks like a town on its way out.
Defences at Rundgate are built to hold, and are kept sound rather than kept for show.
A real body of armed men holds Rundgate's walls, and they carry themselves like men who have done it before.
Children in Rundgate learn the rules about what moves after dark early, and the rules hold.
The watch in Rundgate answers what is brought to it, and does not go looking for what is not.
Prices in Rundgate stay steady in a way that says the town is not living off whatever it last managed to sell.
Magic that is usually needed can be done in Rundgate, by people who know plainly what lies beyond them.
Nobody in Rundgate spends much thought on where the next meal is coming from.
The road to somewhere else runs through Rundgate, and the town has built a modest living out of being passed through.
What Rundgate cannot grow, the road brings in, and the town would not manage long without it.
Quarters in Rundgate have grown large enough that they do not all know one another.
Rundgate has had pressure enough to bend its ties to its neighbours, and they have not bent, the ties here no different from what holds anywhere else.
